answers.explanation: SMTP, IMAP, and POP are application-layer protocols. They ride on TCP at the transport layer.
Every mail protocol in this chapter is a TCP conversation. DHCP and ordinary DNS lookups are the ones that use UDP.
The server is on 67 and the client on 68.
Port 68 for the client, 67 for the server.
MX, mail exchange. Each one names a host and a priority.
An MX must name a real host with its own A or AAAA record, not an alias.
PTR records live under in-addr.arpa and map addresses back to names. Many receivers reject mail from addresses with no PTR.
